# `#[cutile::module]` generated by `macro_rules!` compiles but fails at JIT time

## Summary

A `#[cutile::module]` emitted by a declarative macro compiles and generates launchers, but launching a kernel panics:

```text
__module_ast_self: failed to re-parse captured source text: Error("expected identifier")
```

## Use case

Kernels that differ only in how a tile is loaded, e.g. a dense GEMV and a block-quantized GEMV where the quantized one multiplies by a per-block scale. Sharing the body through `macro_rules!` avoids maintaining several copies of the same loop:

```rust
macro_rules! gemv_module {
    ($module:ident, $entry:ident, [$($params:tt)*], |$pid:ident, $kc:ident| $load:expr) => {
        #[cutile::module]
        mod $module {
            use cutile::core::*;
            #[cutile::entry()]
            pub fn $entry<const B: i32, const BN: i32, const NB: i32>(
                y: &mut Tensor<f32, { [B, BN] }>,
                $($params)*,
                x: &Tensor<f32, { [B, -1, 32] }>,
                blocks: i32,
            ) {
                // shared loop; `let w: Tile<f32, { [BN, NB, 32] }> = $load;`
            }
        }
    };
}

gemv_module!(dense, dense_gemv, [w: &Tensor<bf16, { [-1, -1, 32] }>], |pid, kc| { /* load + convert */ });
gemv_module!(q8, q8_gemv, [qs: &Tensor<i8, { [-1, -1, 32] }>, scales: &Tensor<f16, { [-1, -1] }>], |pid, kc| { /* load * scale */ });
```

## Cause

`emit_module_ast_self_and_registry_entry` (`cutile-macro/src/_module.rs`) stores the module source for the JIT, preferring `Span::source_text()` over `raw_item_source` (`TokenStream::to_string()`). For a module produced by `macro_rules!`, the span points into the macro definition, so the captured text is the unexpanded template (`mod $module { ... $($params)* ... }`), which `syn::parse_str` rejects at launch.

## Proposed fix (unverified)

Use the verbatim source text only when it parses to the same module; otherwise fall back to `raw_item_source`. Macro-generated modules would lose exact line mapping and comments, but would work.

## Related

Passing parameter types through a `$ty:ty` fragment fails earlier, at macro expansion (`Unable to generate launcher: unsupported parameter type`), because the type arrives as an invisible-delimited group. Passing raw tokens (`$($params:tt)*`) avoids it. This may be worth handling or documenting as well.
